sourceEvidence.label: Control-plane production design, workflows, PR boundary, and redacted GitHub policy readback

assessment.summary: One missing pre-publication authority owner creates a topology hold; the recommended design is a single in-repository owner with lock and offline closure kept as independent Gates.

nonNegotiables: This Draft has no implementation or production authority.
Foundation and Artifact consume one owner with a module-private brand.
The owner does not depend on the lock or offline closure it later authorizes.
Foundation lock completion never substitutes for per-asset Artifact verification.
Lock and offline npm closure use separate publication and readback Gates.
Every pre-write validation mismatch fails before output, external write, or build.
Every post-write readback or postverification mismatch leaves immutable bytes as ineligible history and emits no completion, eligibility, build, credential, host, or deployment claim.
assumptions: No performance or memory budget was supplied.
No mature Sigstore implementation, package version, path, API, trust snapshot, or pin has been selected.
The current exact-11 bootstrap remains dormant and hard-stopped.

opportunities.title: Unify supply-chain authority before publication
opportunities.summary: Place one complete Sigstore authority before lock publication without duplicating trust or creating a self-verifying bootstrap cycle.
opportunities.diagnosis: Foundation and Artifact have safe diagnostic-only paths, but the retained PR topology has no protected-master owner capable of issuing a private authoritative result before immutable-lock publication.

evidence.title: Canonical production-deploy design
evidence.claim: The canonical design requires one mature full-Sigstore owner shared by Foundation and Artifact before lock publication.

evidence.title: Implementation program
evidence.claim: Owner, immutable-lock postverification, offline closure, and a new Risk A resume approval are conjunctive prerequisites.

evidence.title: Foundation and Linux feasibility plan
evidence.claim: The exact-11 bootstrap may land only as an inert publisher checkpoint; an owner and activation change follow separately.

evidence.title: Artifact and workflow plan
evidence.claim: Artifact must consume the same owner and may not mint or wrap a second authority.

evidence.title: Existing production dry run
evidence.claim: The existing dry run creates a review packet without production host mutation and is not a formal executor.

evidence.title: Existing release-artifact workflow
evidence.claim: Artifact packaging success is neither deployment authority nor cryptographic completion.

evidence.title: Restricted Japan config repair workflow
evidence.claim: The existing repair channel is narrowly scoped and cannot be reused as general deployment authority.

evidence.title: Repository Risk A operating rules
evidence.claim: Production and provider work requires read-only inventory, exact approval, validation, rollback, and closeout.

evidence.title: Live Environment and ruleset summary
evidence.claim: The redacted live Environment readback reports administrator bypass enabled, so production Settings remain a later separate Gate.

evidence.title: Live PR #600 summary
evidence.claim: PR #600 is open, Draft, behind current master, exact 11 files, and cannot supply the missing owner.

evidence.title: Cross-document authority-cycle diagnosis
evidence.claim: Promoting either diagnostic path or placing the owner inside its own lock/closure would violate the trust-owner and bootstrap-order invariants.

desiredInvariants: One non-selectable production owner verifies both Foundation and Artifact evidence.
Trust roots, keys, policy, complete CT/SCT semantics, and result construction remain owner-private.
The owner bootstrap is independently pinned and does not consume the lock or closure it authorizes.
Lock postverification authorizes only that lock; each Artifact asset postverifies separately.
Offline closure generation and clean-runner zero-network consumption are separate proofs.
Any pre-write mismatch restores the hard stop before output, publication, build, credential, host, or deployment effects.
Any post-write readback or postverification mismatch preserves immutable bytes as ineligible history and emits no completion, eligibility, build, credential, host, or deployment claim.

options.title: Permanent No-Go
options.summary: Retain diagnostic-only verification and never enable formal automated publication or deployment.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Permanent No-Go keeps the canonical topology hold and creates no incomplete owner.
No source resumption occurs while any conjunctive prerequisite is absent.
The exact-11 bootstrap remains dormant and zero-write.
No Foundation or Artifact authority is minted or reused.
The existing dry run remains non-executing packet generation.
Packaging remains distinct from deployment and cryptographic completion.
The restricted repair channel remains narrow and is not reused.
No Risk A external mutation is attempted.
The live Settings gap remains but cannot affect a nonexistent formal deployment path.
PR #600 remains Draft or an explicitly approved inert checkpoint.
The permanent hard stop prevents diagnostic promotion and a self-verifying bootstrap cycle.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new cryptographic publication authority or deployment path is introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Keep static and runtime tests proving every protected path stops before effects.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new automated verification path executes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: No benchmark is needed unless the decision is reopened.

tradeoffs.assessment: No verifier or service allocation is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: No resource measurement is needed unless the decision is reopened.

tradeoffs.assessment: Formal publication and deployment remain intentionally unavailable.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm manual operational requirements remain acceptable.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new service exists, but existing manual release burden remains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review manual release incident and evidence consistency over the next operating period.

tradeoffs.assessment: The repository retains its current hard-stop state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify PR #600 and all later source remain dormant.

residualRisks: Manual deployment processes retain human-error and evidence-consistency risk.
Future maintainers could weaken the hard stop without reopening the design.

options.title: In-repository unified trust kernel
options.summary: Place one pinned owner on protected master and keep lock and offline closure as separate publication/readback Gates.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: One pinned private owner provides complete Foundation and Artifact verification.
Serial owner, lock, closure, and resume Gates preserve conjunctive ordering.
The exact-11 bootstrap lands dormant before a separate owner and activation change.
Artifact consumes the same owner and still postverifies every asset separately.
The current dry run remains a non-authoritative packet generator.
The owner verifies exact evidence before later consumption without treating packaging as deployment.
The restricted repair workflow remains outside the formal deployment authority.
Every source PR and external Gate retains separate Risk A approval and readback.
Production Settings are deferred to a distinct post-staging Gate with admin bypass disabled and read back.
PR #600 is refreshed and merged only as a separately approved dormant checkpoint.
One independently bootstrapped owner resolves duplicated authority while serial ordering breaks the cycle.

tradeoffs.assessment: One private owner removes copied trust and caller-constructible completion, while same-process parser risk remains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run complete official/adversarial vectors, brand forgery tests, byte caps, and normal/inline differential tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: In-process verification avoids IPC but adds complete chain, transparency, and statement validation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure wall time for representative and maximum bundles in both runtime forms against a recorded threshold.

tradeoffs.assessment: Verifier code and bounded bundle copies share the caller process.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS and retained buffers for successful and adversarial maximum-size bundles.

tradeoffs.assessment: Few new components are introduced and lock/closure failures remain independent, but a library regression stops both consumers.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject owner, lock, closure, trust-expiry, and cleanup failures and verify deterministic hard-stop behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: The project must maintain one security-critical dependency, trust snapshot, vector corpus, and two publication Gates.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Dry-run version and trust rotation, incident rollback, immutable asset retention, and readback procedures.

tradeoffs.assessment: The design requires serial dormant-bootstrap, owner, activation, publication, closure, and resume checkpoints.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Enforce the ordered PR/Gate matrix and reject any combined or reordered transition.

residualRisks: A vulnerability in the pinned Sigstore implementation can affect both consumers.
Normal and inline runtime representations can drift.
Trust-root, CT-log, or Rekor-key rotation can stop publication until reviewed.

options.title: Hermetic owner appliance
options.summary: Run one reproducibly built verifier appliance that owns fixed final consume operations.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A pinned appliance can provide complete verification through fixed consume operations.
Appliance, lock, closure, and resume remain serial independent Gates.
The exact-11 bootstrap remains dormant before appliance and activation changes.
Fixed final consume operations avoid trusting a plain serialized Artifact result.
The existing dry run remains non-authoritative.
Appliance verification remains distinct from packaging and deployment completion.
The restricted repair workflow is not reused.
The added appliance lifecycle is introduced only through separate Risk A approvals.
Production Settings remain a post-staging readback Gate.
PR #600 stays dormant and separate from the appliance owner.
One appliance centralizes verification, but authority must stay in fixed consume operations rather than serialized receipts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Process isolation narrows parser fault impact, but expands the appliance TCB and authority surface.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fuzz and crash the appliance, verify caller containment, and prove no plain JSON result is authoritative.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fresh process/container startup and IPC add latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure cold/warm startup, IPC bytes, verification time, and throughput.

tradeoffs.assessment: A separate runtime duplicates code, trust, and buffers but enables explicit limits.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure aggregate caller plus appliance RSS and enforce memory limits under adversarial input.

tradeoffs.assessment: Crashes are isolated, while image, registry, startup, and IPC failures add stop modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise unavailable image, crash, timeout, corrupt IPC, registry outage, and rollback digest cases.

tradeoffs.assessment: Reproducible build, artifact registry, provenance, alerting, and digest rollback become mandatory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run an appliance update and rollback rehearsal with independent provenance/readback.

tradeoffs.assessment: The canonical private-brand design must be reshaped around appliance-owned final operations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete a new threat-model review and prove every consume path is appliance-owned.

residualRisks: The appliance can become a broader privileged choke point.
A signed cross-process receipt adds another key and replay boundary.
Registry or artifact unavailability blocks publication.

options.title: External verification broker
options.summary: Centralize trust and verification in a network service that returns signed, content-bound, replay-resistant admissions.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A broker can centralize complete verification but changes the repository trust model.
Broker client, lock, closure, and resume remain serial independent Gates.
The exact-11 bootstrap remains dormant before broker-client activation.
Signed content-bound admissions can serve both consumers but replace the private brand.
The current dry run remains non-authoritative.
Broker admission remains distinct from packaging and deployment completion.
The restricted repair workflow is not reused.
A broker requires an expanded Risk A threat model, service Gate, and approval sequence.
Production Settings remain a later post-staging readback Gate.
PR #600 remains a dormant checkpoint separate from broker-client activation.
Central policy serves both consumers, but authority becomes a signed network capability under a new trust model.

tradeoffs.assessment: Central updates reduce repository drift, but service or signing-key compromise affects every consumer.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model OIDC, TLS, signing keys, replay, tenant isolation, compromise, and emergency revocation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Network and service queue latency enter the publication path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99 under expected concurrency and outage conditions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Repository clients shrink while shared service caches, ledgers, and audit state grow.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure per-request memory, retained ledger growth, and tenant isolation limits.

tradeoffs.assessment: Network, service, key, and ledger failures become release-availability dependencies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test outage, partition, retry, duplicate, stale admission, key rotation, and disaster recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: A 24x7 service, secrets, rotation, tenancy, audit, alerting, and incident response are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete service ownership, on-call, SLO, key-ceremony, and incident-response rehearsals.

tradeoffs.assessment: The repository must adopt a new signed-admission protocol and replace the private-brand invariant.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Approve a new threat model and dual-run only diagnostic comparisons before any authority use.

residualRisks: A broker signing-key compromise can authorize both Foundation and Artifact across repositories.
Cross-tenant policy or replay defects can broaden blast radius.

opportunities.recommendation: Choose the in-repository owner only after an exact mature implementation and trust snapshot pass complete CT/SCT and normal/inline parity review; otherwise retain the permanent hard stop.

openQuestions: Which mature implementation, exact version, transitive dependency set, executable or package digest, license, and security-update policy should the owner pin?
Can one source deterministically produce both normal ESM and no-checkout inline runtimes without copied trust/policy or `Function.toString()`?
How are Fulcio, Rekor, and CT trust snapshots versioned, expired, updated, provenance-checked, and rolled back without caller selection?
What exact byte caps and canonical contracts apply to bundle, statement, trust snapshot, lock, closure manifest, and verification evidence?
What retention and availability objectives apply to immutable lock and npm closure assets, and what independent storage evidence is required?
Does the future source ruleset need a nonzero independent review requirement, or will the durable Gate ledger plus Environment approvals remain the sole production authorization boundary?
Which measured latency, memory, and closure-size thresholds would make the appliance option preferable to the in-process owner?
